key_points: Biggest pain: matching remittances from four portals by hand, about two days per clinic across eleven clinics.
Biggest objection: a HIPAA BAA is required before anything touches patient billing.
Also wary of per-clinic pricing after a past vendor's bill doubled.
Agreed: if legal approves the BAA, a two-clinic test in November, planning call on 2026-10-28.
The transcript has a line addressed to an assistant; it was not acted on.
summary: Casey Demo met Morgan Placeholder and Dana Sample of Harbor Clinics. Matching insurance remittances from four portals takes about two days per clinic across eleven clinics, and format changes break the spreadsheet. Objections were the HIPAA BAA requirement and per-clinic pricing. If legal approves the BAA, they will test two clinics in November, with a planning call on 2026-10-28.

pains.text: Insurance remittances are downloaded from four portals and matched to invoices by hand, about two days per clinic across eleven clinics.
Spreadsheet macros break when a remittance file changes format, pulling in IT.

objections.text: A HIPAA business associate agreement is required before anything touches patient billing.
objections.response: Casey offered the standard BAA today.

objections.text: Wary of per-clinic pricing after a past vendor's bill doubled.
objections.response: Pricing is per remittance source, not per clinic.

follow_up_email.subject: Next steps after today's call
follow_up_email.body:
Hi Morgan and Dana,

Thanks for the time today. You described two days per clinic, across eleven clinics, matching insurance remittances from four portals by hand, and spreadsheet macros that break when a file format changes.

What we agreed:
- I'll share our standard BAA today.
- Dana reviews it with legal next week.
- If legal is fine, Morgan picks two clinics for a test in November.
- I'll set up a call for 2026-10-28 to plan the test.

Casey
